To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interdiffusion effects on bandstructure in HgCdTe/CdTe SL structures for VLWIR applications are investigated.
the interdiffusion effects can be controlled by annealing time and the optimized superlattice structure can be used as a viable alternative to HgCdTe for VLWIR applications.
interdiffusion in HgTe/CdtTe (112)B superlattices can be controlled to achieve better cut-off wavelength control and larger electron effective mass compared to the corresponding bulk HgCdTe absorber.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of HgTe/Cdt e superlattice structures for use in very long wavelength infrared imaging focal plane arrays.
the development of VLWIR photodetectors using superlattices, which are more suitable for high performance imaging applications.
optimizing SL absorbers in order to improve the performance of VLWIR photodetectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for VLWIR applications, a SL structure is a viable alternative to the HgCdTe absorber, and it has a potential for better control of the bandgap and lower dark current.

the interdiffusion of the SL absorber is a viable option for VLWIR focal plane array applications, with an added benefit of a higher sensitivity to well width variation compared to a HgCd _{x} Te _{1−x} absorber.
, by appropriate optimization of the SL parameters and growth conditions, it is possible, in principle, to achieve the same performance in a superlattice structure as a HgCd alloy structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interdiffusion in SL structures is a useful tool to achieve better control of the bandstructure and hence the device characteristics.
, with appropriate optimization of the superstructure, it is possible that a SL structure can be used in the VLWIR region.

, by appropriate optimization, the superlattice structure can be used as an absorber for VLWIR imaging applications, with the added advantages of reduced sensitivity to well width variations and lower tunneling dark currents.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by optimizing interdiffusion in the superlattice structure, it is possible achieve better control of the bandstructure in SL absorbers compared to HgCdTe alloys, and thus achieve better performance in VLWIR photodetectors.
, with appropriate annealing, the superlattice can be designed to have similar cut-off wavelength as a HgCdte alloy absorber with a larger Hgte well width.
SL absorbers have the potential to be used as an alternative to HgCdTe alloys in the VLWIR region.
